# Brett Boggs

> Site of Brett Boggs: operations and systems for small businesses, in person around St. Louis and St. Charles County, Missouri, and remote anywhere; co-founder of Datum, an all-in-one construction management platform; and a photographer. This file is a curated, factual index for machine readers. If anything here conflicts with a page on the site, the page wins.

Contact: hello@brettboggs.dev · GitHub: https://github.com/brettmboggs

## Operations and systems for small businesses

From the homepage (https://brettboggs.dev/): Brett builds small businesses one system they own in place of a stack of subscriptions, so they can cancel the rest. The business keeps the code, the data, the domain and every login, with a handover document. The homepage has a calculator for a business's yearly software and lost-hours overhead. Based in O'Fallon, Missouri; in person across St. Charles County and the St. Louis area, by phone or video anywhere.

Brett works alone, on purpose: there is no company in the middle, so what he builds belongs to the client, and the person who built it is the person who answers. He spent ten years running operations (a dealership service lane, car washes up to a district of eight locations) before building software, and starts every engagement by finding where work gets stuck.

Prices:
- A first look is free (20 minutes).
- An operations review is $350 for 90 minutes and a written plan, credited toward any project.
- One process automated or rebuilt: $1,500 to $3,000, fixed quote.
- A full system replacing a booking or field-service app and parts of accounting: $5,000 to $12,000, fixed quote.
- Websites with Google profile setup: from $1,500, no hosting fee.
- Keeping a system running: from $400 a month.

How he helps (https://brettboggs.dev/help/):
- [Operations review](https://brettboggs.dev/help/operations-review/): ninety minutes and a written plan of what to fix first.
- [Software your business owns](https://brettboggs.dev/help/custom-software/): one system in place of a stack of subscriptions.
- [Automating the busywork](https://brettboggs.dev/help/automations/): missed-call text-back, quote follow-ups, reminders, orders into the books.
- [Websites and Google profiles](https://brettboggs.dev/help/websites/): fast sites the business owns, and Google profiles that are filled in.
- [AI, where it actually helps](https://brettboggs.dev/help/ai-for-small-business/): plain advice and setup, only where it saves time or money.
- [Keeping it running](https://brettboggs.dev/help/keeping-it-running/): hosting, fixes, edits and one improvement a quarter.
- [Why it's one person](https://brettboggs.dev/help/one-person/) and [Questions](https://brettboggs.dev/help/questions/).

## Datum

Datum (https://datumci.com) is one system for running a construction company: projects, people, equipment, safety, and money in one place. Brett co-founded it and builds the product end to end as full-stack engineer: design, frontend, backend, architecture, security, infrastructure, and release.

Shipped, as counted on https://brettboggs.dev/work/datum/:
- 2,259 HTTP endpoints across 394 backend services
- 1,031 tables in Azure SQL, behind 558 tracked migrations
- 332 screens and 392 shared components in React
- 132 standard operating procedures, automated end to end
- Tenant isolation enforced at the query layer, role based access through Entra ID
- An ERP adapter framework with a durable writeback queue, normalizing phase codes and cost types
- GDPR deletion and data subject export across three previously unconnected identity systems
- A React Native app through TestFlight, an Outlook add-in, CI/CD into Azure with health checks and uptime monitoring

## Before Datum

- Operations Manager, Providence Capital (real estate investment), 2025 to present: intake-to-close documentation for 200+ active files, automated routing, correspondence templates, live reporting.
- Area Manager, Tidal Wave Auto Spa, 2022 to 2025: eight locations, forty-plus people, centralized records, automated incident intake.
- General Manager, Tidal Wave Auto Spa, 2020 to 2022: a $2.1M annual budget, KPI dashboards, two years of 100% compliance audits.
- Associate degree, General Studies, St. Louis Community College.

## Work

- [Datum](https://brettboggs.dev/work/datum/): One system for running a construction company.
- [Photography](https://brettboggs.dev/work/photography/): Commercial, live music, and product photography, 2021 to 2023.
- [Websites](https://brettboggs.dev/work/websites/): Sites for small businesses. Mattress Concepts, a mattress store and workshop in High Ridge, off Wix with a quote form that draws the mattress to scale. Lauren Becherer Pottery (https://laurenbechererpottery.com), handmade ceramics built around 360 degree turntable photography, and Knock Em' Down Detailing, a mobile auto and marine detailer in St. Louis: a new site, a new logo and brand kit, online quotes and booking, and an iPhone app to run the business.

## Apps

- [Slumbio](https://brettboggs.dev/slumbio/): An iPhone sleep app, released September 2026. Thirty-three of its thirty-five sounds are built as they play, so there is no loop to hear. Breathing sessions, a sunrise alarm, a sleep timer, and no network code in the app at all. On the App Store at https://apps.apple.com/app/id6808987732
- [Ladle](https://brettboggs.dev/ladle/): An iPhone app for recipes, wherever they come from: scanned off a card with the camera, shared from Safari, or typed in. Cook mode takes voice commands, a pantry tracks what is in the kitchen, and nothing leaves the phone.

## Lab

- [The MacArthur](https://brettboggs.dev/lab/trra/): A rail bridge approach in St. Louis, rebuilt to scale from OpenStreetMap and USGS public domain data, with an interactive model of the job.
- [The Field](https://brettboggs.dev/lab/field/): A prairie run on the GPU. Every blade is a spring in a compute shader, and the cursor is weather.
- [Keepsake](https://brettboggs.dev/lab/keepsake/): A seeded drawing, deterministic from its hash, different for every visitor.
- [Sprout Siege](https://brettboggs.dev/lab/sprout-siege/): An idle farm game for iOS, built around a simulation core that never touches the screen.
- [The Ridge](https://brettboggs.dev/lab/ridge/): A golden hour flyover, rendered in Blender and scrubbed by scroll. It opened the front page until October 2026.
- [The Underground](https://brettboggs.dev/lab/underground/): The same ground as the Ridge, cut open six metres to rock. Roots grow as you scroll.
- [The Bridge](https://brettboggs.dev/lab/bridge/): A cable-stayed crossing that surveys, drafts and builds itself as you scroll. Datum's first landing film.
- [The Drafting Film](https://brettboggs.dev/lab/drafting-film/): A highway underpass you draft by scrolling. It ran Datum's landing page for one night.
